Four, with two in each anther lobe

stem: Pollen grains are found well preserved as fossils in very old rocks. Which property of the pollen grain best explains this?

Its germ pores close tightly after the pollen is shed
Its exine has sporopollenin, which no enzyme degrades

stem: A mature pollen grain at the time of shedding has one large cell with abundant food reserve and an irregular nucleus, and two small cells lying in its cytoplasm. Which interpretation is correct?

stem: Why does self-pollination not lead to seed formation in a self-incompatible species?

The anthers of such plants never produce any viable pollen grains at all.
The stigma becomes receptive only after all of its own pollen is shed.

explanation: Correct option: (D). With no meiosis and no fertilisation, the embryo carries only the mother plant's diploid genetic material and is a clone of it. stem: Read the case 'The cost of hybrid seed'. How would transferring apomictic genes into a hybrid variety help the farmer?
options: Hybrid plants would become self-incompatible and would always outcross.
Seeds would form without fertilisation, so hybrid traits stay fixed.
Fruits would become seedless, so no seed would ever need to be bought.
The chromosome number would double, making the hybrids more vigorous.
explanation: Correct option: (B). Apomictic seeds form without meiosis and fertilisation, so the progeny are genetically identical to the hybrid and do not segregate; the farmer can save seed and keep using it year after year. Self-incompatibility would not stop segregation, seedless fruits would leave no seed to sow, and apomixis does not double chromosome numbers.
